title: Reproducing Stesmans and Afanas'ev 1996: Pb defects released from hydrogen and created by vacuum anneals

sample.paper: “commercial two-side polished float zone (111)Si wafers (10 Ω cm, p-type) of 2 inch diameter”; slices 2×9 mm²
sample.ours: FAMILY: Si_Planar; ORIENTATION: Si111; DOPING recorded (no program reads it)
the 1965 growth law at 1 atm (1.1 cannot be written), time chosen for 42 nm
sample.note: The oxidation time is not stated.

sample.paper: “fully passivate the Pb bath … as affirmed by ESR diagnosis”
sample.ours: RUN Passivation … AMBIENT pure_H2 (1 atm, not 1.1)

sample.paper: two-side polished slices; whether both faces are oxidized and counted is not stated

history.item: Dry oxidation at about 970 °C in 1.1 atm O2 to about 42 nm
history.paper: “thermally oxidized at ∼970 °C (1.1 atm O2; 99.999%) to an oxide thickness dox ∼42 nm”; caption: “1.1 atm O2, ∼967 °C, dox ≈ 42 nm”
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 1900 TEMP 970->970 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Temperature, pressure and thickness are stated; the time is not. Ours is what the predictor's 1965 growth law needs for 42 nm at 1 atm. 1.1 atm cannot be written: the runtime refuses a partial pressure above 1 atm.

history.ours: RUN Cool DURATION 600 TEMP 970->25 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Gas, rate and end temperature are ours.

history.item: Hydrogen passivation, 405 °C, about 40 min, 1.1 atm H2
history.paper: “followed by a ∼40 min treatment in H2 (1.1 atm; 99.9999%) at 405 °C in order to fully passivate the Pb bath (equation (1)), as affirmed by ESR diagnosis”
history.ours: RUN Passivation DURATION 2400 TEMP 405->405 AMBIENT pure_H2
history.note: Written as pure H2 at 1 atm: the runtime refuses a partial pressure above 1 atm. In the equilibrium program 1.1 atm would change the uncapped share by a factor 1/√1.1. Heat-up and cool-down not stated.

history.paper: “Samples were than submitted to a 62 min anneal in a diffusion-pumped vacuum (⩽4 × 10−7 Torr) at selected temperatures T, in the range 480 to 1135 °C.” “The accuracy reached on T is ⩽0.3%.”
history.ours: RUN VacuumAnneal DURATION 3720 TEMP 520->520 AMBIENT vacuum
history.note: Vacuum written without a pressure; no program reads one. Heat-up and cool-down of the 2 × 9 mm² slices are not stated.

history.item: K-band ESR (20.6 GHz) at 4.3 K, B ∥ [111], against a Si:P standard
history.paper: “Conventional absorption-mode ESR (∼20.6 GHz) measurements [2] were carried out at 4.3 K.”; “The absolute spin density accuracy is estimated at ∼10%, while the relative accuracy may be better than 5%.”
history.ours: no observable reports a spin density in cm⁻²; compared as a share of N0 with the computed share of uncapped bonds

history.paper: “one freshly standardly oxidized sample submitted at once to a high-T vacuum anneal at 968 °C for 1 h … alternating full passivation in H2 followed by a 62 min vacuum anneal … at incremental T steps in the range 480–967 °C”
history.ours: RUN Creation 968 °C 1 h; RUN Repassivation; RUN VacuumAnneal at T. Earlier cycles left out
history.note: Each cycle ends in full passivation, so earlier cycles matter only through created Pb, which no program has.

history.paper: “the very same effects have been observed when, instead of vacuum, post-oxidation annealing is carried out in inert ambient, i.e., N2 or Ar”
